findings.title: $168M of longs liquidated, open interest still at the 98th percentile
findings.lean_why: Price is down 9.4% in 30 days while leverage grew by a tenth and accounts lean long; another drop would force market-sold liquidations that amplify it.
findings.what: Sunday's drop cleared a batch of longs, but leverage as a whole did not retreat: price fell 9.4% in 30 days while total perp open interest rose 10.6%, at the 98th percentile since 2021 (Coinalyze, Nov 8).
findings.why: Basis: no signal captured this; taken from deriv.liq_vol, oi_hist, ls_acct and funding_multi in the brief. Liquidations: Nov 8 longs $168M, shorts $8.3M, 93% longs; 7-day longs $491M (Coinalyze five venues, actual records, under-reported). Open interest: 339,077 BTC vs 340,639 the day before, only 0.5% lower after the flush, +2.1% over 7 days. Cross-check: Binance long-account share 75.5% (96th percentile), Bybit 70.6%; funding on the old three-venue basis 9.98% → 6.45%, OKX now 2.30%, so longs pay much less and the rush to go long has cooled, but the positions remain. Contradiction: Hyperliquid's top 2,000 accounts hold 14,082 BTC short vs 9,439 BTC long, so big accounts lean short and the long build is in smaller accounts.
findings.alt: Part of the open-interest rise may be basis trades (long spot, short perp) or hedging shorts, not all longs; the long-account share counts accounts, not position size. Coinalyze's Binance liquidation feed pushes one record per second, so totals run low: good for long vs short, not for size. Big Hyperliquid accounts may be market makers or hedgers. Funding became a five-venue weighted figure on Nov 9; comparisons with yesterday use the three-venue basis.
findings.history: High long-account share (≥ 90th percentile) occurred 27 times: 90 days later price was higher 11 times, median −4.5%, versus 53% and +2.0% normally (Coinalyze, since 2021); most recently Oct 31 at 74.0%. Contracts were added over time, so part of the long-term open-interest rise is new contracts; discount the percentile.
findings.so: What changed is the cost of leverage: funding fell about 3.5 points in a day, the long rush cooled. What did not change is the positions: open interest barely fell after the flush, and the estimated long-liquidation bands at 72,200–73,300 (−2.8%, about 18.1K BTC) and 70,000–72,100 (−5.0%) remain (estimate, Coinalyze seven exchanges). Conditional: a move into those bands would trigger forced long selling at market, which can accelerate a drop. Market stage and exit framework unchanged.
findings.next: By Nov 15: open interest at or below 322,000 BTC (about −5%) would show leverage really retreating, refuting this; 7-day long liquidations above $800M would show leverage being flushed by force rather than cut voluntarily, confirming it.

findings.title: Bottom combo fired, but loss-taking is under 40% of the June low
findings.lean_why: Past bottom combos did better than normal over 90 days but worse over 30, and loss-taking this time is shallow, so sellers have not truly capitulated; the two sides offset.
findings.what: Our in-house selling pressure stayed at 100 and momentum quality fell to 0.25, so the bottom combo fired (Daybreak, daily closes only, Nov 8). But on-chain loss-taking is shallow: the latest realized-loss peak is only 4.82 bp of market cap, against 13.2 at the Jun 30 low (Bitview).
findings.why: Basis: no signal captured this; taken from chips.stress and onchain.rloss in the brief. Momentum quality 0.30 → 0.25 as the 21-day return t-stat weakened again; the fifth losing week. Cross-check: 73.8% of short-term holders at a loss, 26.2% in profit, a 30-day low (Bitview); STH-SOPR 0.9931, third day below 1 (CheckOnChain); short-term holder realized loss 4,177 → 3,875 BTC, profit 3,071 BTC (CheckOnChain Nov 8). Contradiction: more holders are underwater on paper while realized loss-taking shrinks; the Nov 6 realized-loss peak of 4.82 bp is a little below the Sep 15 peak of 5.41, flagged flat, not a divergence. The other side: LTH-SOPR 0.9701 → 0.9393, so long-term holders who sell are also selling at a loss (Bitview), and 35.6% of 30-day realized losses came from 1–2 year holders.
findings.alt: Selling pressure uses closes only, so a slow grind lower also fills it; 0.25 versus 0.3 is not a meaningful difference. Realized loss and SOPR are per-UTXO, not entity-adjusted, so exchange wallet reshuffles get mixed in; in the ETF era much turnover happens in the stock market off-chain, so on-chain loss-taking may simply run shallower.
findings.history: Since 2012 the bottom combo has fired 21 times: 30 days later up 11 times, median +0.3% (normal 57%, +3.2%); 90 days up 13 times, median +14.7% (normal 60%, +9.9%); by the end of the combo 13 gains, median +4.2%, average 40 days, with a median 9.3% dip along the way. By era: 2012–2017 3 of 6, 2018–2022 6 of 9, 2023–2026 4 of 6; after 2022/04 price fell another 51.5%, and both 2014 cases fell over 40% more.
findings.so: Logic chain: price-based weakness has maxed out (A happened), so the bottom combo fired; but on-chain there is no June-style concentrated capitulation (B has not happened), so we cannot say sellers have given up. This is not a buy signal: past 30-day results were worse than normal, with a median 9.3% dip during the combo. Market stage and exit framework unchanged.
findings.next: By Nov 15: short-term holder realized loss above 5,000 BTC, or STH-SOPR below 0.985, would show loss-taking widening, refuting "shallow loss-taking".

findings.title: The three big buyer groups' costs stack at 75–79K, all underwater now
findings.lean_why: Short-term holders, Strategy and ETF holders all have their cost above price, so rallies there meet break-even selling; below, supply is thin down to 64K with no thick bid.
findings.what: Question: ahead of Monday's open, where is break-even supply above and support below? The answer is that cost sits overhead: short-term holder cost 75,881, Strategy's average 75,451 and the estimated ETF holder cost 79,039 are all above the 74,738 close (Bitview, TechFlow, The Block estimate, Nov 5–8).
findings.why: Participants and cost map (CheckOnChain actual coin age, Nov 8): short-term holders 3.720M BTC at an average 75,219; the three thickest bands are 76K (624K), 80K (531K) and 62K (478K); long-term holder cost 48,833 (Bitview), still deep in profit. The true market mean at 77,563 is 3.8% above. Two points in time: 30 days ago short-term holders held 3.616M BTC at 74,205 (Bitview actual); now about 100K more, with cost about 1,000 higher; new unmoved coins concentrate at 76K and 80K (estimate; total off by 0.4%, 8.0% misplaced). Behavior: long-term holder 30-day net position −102,380 → −75,898 BTC (bitcoin-data Nov 7), net selling narrowing; LTH-SOPR 0.9393, so long-term sellers are also at a loss; ETFs lost about $1.28B in a week, the highest-cost group trimming.
findings.alt: ETF holder cost is our estimate from flows ÷ close, ex-GBTC; Strategy's cost is a company-reported figure, and paper losses are not sales. CheckOnChain and Bitview are per-UTXO, not entity-adjusted, so exchange wallet moves count as turnover; URPD lags 1–2 days. Long-term net position changes also include coins aging past 155 days.
findings.history: Price near the thickest short-term pile (±3%) for 4 days and near short-term holder cost for 4 days (signals); day 398 after the cycle top, where the prior three cycles sat 74.7%–81.6% below their tops versus −40.1% now; only three cycles of sample.
findings.so: Logic chain: all three main buyer groups are underwater (A happened), so a bounce into 75.5–79K meets break-even supply first; long-term holder net selling is narrowing (B did not worsen), so old coins are not the main sellers. Scenario (conditional, CheckOnChain Nov 8): at a 70,000 close 2.660M short-term holder BTC would be at a loss, at 66,000 only 2.709M, jumping to 3.109M only at 64,000; long-term holder coins at a loss rise from 5.706M at 74,000 to 6.793M at 66,000. With no thick cost zone between 74K and 66K, price tends to move fast through thin supply. Market stage and exit framework unchanged.
findings.next: By Nov 15: a close back above 76,000, above both short-term holder and Strategy cost, refutes this; a close below 72,200 (under the 200-day average and the estimated liquidation band) confirms the overhead cost has turned into resistance.
